sections.html: Channa marulius comes from India. The normal size of the species is about 50 cm. The largest documented catch was a specimen about 120 cm long that weighed 13.6 kg; allegedly there has also been a 183 cm specimen weighing a good 30 kg.
Because of their size, Channa marulius are reserved for owners of very large aquariums, zoos and display aquariums. Their final size is the main restriction on their suitability as an aquarium fish.
India is its homeland. There, huge, tame C. marulius live in ponds in sacred temple precincts and are worshipped and fed by believers. They will take rice balls from the hand.
These are predatory fish. Rice is not an adequate food for them.

In the aquarium, Channa marulius are pleasant contemporaries, and their aggression potential is low compared to other snakeheads. This changes at breeding time, when they form pairs and sustainably defend a nest around the numerous brood. They have quite decent teeth and are fearless.

Young animals are coloured completely differently from adults. While in juvenile dress they are schooling fish. When they lose the yellow longitudinal stripe they enter puberty, in which every conspecific is seen as a food competitor; during this phase it is impossible to keep more than one specimen in the aquarium. Only when they reach sexual maturity do they become interested in conspecifics again. These phases are typical for large predatory fishes.
